reviews.text: I rang for an emergency appointment for my dog, he had never attended before but the receptionist was so understanding and accepted him straight away, she told us to come down right away and an amazing vet seen him within 10mins. Between the lovely receptionist and the amazing vet they turned an emergency for us into a relaxed appointment, they listened they took such good care of our dog and we left so happy. I’ll be transferring my other dog to this vet from now on. Highly recommend

Unfortunately I wouldn’t recommend, I brought my dog here as we recently moved to the area, they wanted all her records before seeing her which is fair however I booked her in for a booster kennel cough but the vet gave her a full dose (up the nose) I thought it was odd & said ohh that’s new, she usually gets a needle, she said “needles are just for boosters” I told her it was suppose to be a booster but she ignored me, assuming this was more expensive. she didn’t show any sort of interest or even pet my My dog even though I had told her she was nervous, our old vet would give treats & pet her to make her feel less scared but no bedside manner here, only asked “if she bites”.
She had a lump on her neck which I asked her to look at, she said she would take a biopsy & send away, told me it would be a week & she would call me, when she took the biopsy myself & partner couldn’t see anything on the slide, she said they only need a small bit & it was fine, paid €280, waited a week, no phone call, called the clinic several times for the next week & an extremely rude receptionist told me the vet would call me when she had time, eventually she called me back after a 2 week wait, said the results were inconclusive as the sample wasn’t enough & that we would have to repeat the test, I told her that we hadn’t seen anything on the slide she sent so I wasn’t surprised, she told me to come back in & redo the test & that we would have to pay another €120 for a second time, I told her it should have been done properly the first time & she told me they could do it for half price but it wasn’t parented they would get a result so We could do a different test for €180, absolute scam, so they wanted €400 for a biopsy that should have cost €120 had it been done properly, unfortunately they care more about money than the pets they are supposed to be treating, save yourself some stress & money & go elsewhere!

We regularly visit this veterinary clinic with our dog and always pay for all procedures. Our dog is insured, so after each visit the clinic is supposed to complete and send the insurance claim forms to Allianz so we can receive reimbursement.

Unfortunately, every single time there are huge delays. We provide all documents on time, but then have to spend weeks or even months calling repeatedly to ask why the forms still have not been sent, preventing us from getting our money back from the insurance company.

Most recently, we submitted the forms over 6 weeks ago and, despite multiple phone calls, nothing has been done. When I called again yesterday to ask about the status, I was spoken to quite dismissively and simply told that they have “a large backlog.”

I understand that clinics can be busy, but clients should not have to constantly chase staff to complete basic administrative responsibilities. We are very disappointed with the communication and the way this situation has been handled.

Sadly, Our beautiful Mabel & ourselves were badly let down by this practice.  We had been long time clients. When Mabel developed a bad cough, retching at the end and a small solid lump on her hip, we brought her here for a full examination.  She was diagnosed with kennel cough & lump called insignificant.
2 weeks later we returned because the cough had worsened and the lump had doubled. The diagnosis remained the same. Asked for bloods to be done.
A week later we returned and saw a different vet, Conor. He told us the blood results were clear, we asked about doing imaging, he told us we would be throwing our money away. When we asked how confident he was with the diagnosis,  he laughed and said he had been in this game over 35 years. He also told us to stop bringing Mabel in over niggling little things, he said if you keep looking for things, we'll find them and regarding the lump, he said sure we all get lumps and bumps as we get older.
Still concerned, we brought Mabel to another vet. Who diagnosed an enlarged heart. Started meds . We still weren't satisfied as symptoms were not clearing up . Went to killester vets. They carried out full imaging and biopsies.  Mabel was diagnosed with tumors in her lung, on hip and lower leg, it was an agressive cancer.
She sadly passed away last Saturday.
Had O'Scanaill vets taken our concerns seriously they would have done a full investigation including imaging which they did not .
We are absolutely sickened by the treatment we received from O'Scanaill vets. While this practice maybe fine for routine check ups, we felt there was a serious lack of care and attention given to both the animals and the concerns of their owners.

After several visits with my dog, I asked multiple times if everything was fine with her health. I even pointed out a lump on her abdomen and specifically asked them to check it. Each time, I was told that everything was fine and that there was nothing to worry about.

However, when I later went to another veterinarian for a second opinion, the diagnosis was completely different: my dog had a tumor.

This situation has been extremely upsetting. Unfortunately, the clinic has not taken any responsibility for what happened, which has forced me to start legal action.

Because of this experience, I would not recommend this clinic to other pet owners.
(Thank you so much Connor)

I brought my dog, Judite, for an evaluation before a dental cleaning procedure. When I arrived at the consultation, I had difficulty understanding the veterinarian, Dr. Glen Daly, because I don’t speak English. She seemed visibly uncomfortable having to explain or repeat anything and was impatient from the beginning. I tried to explain that Judite had seemed strange two days earlier—breathing heavily and feeling overheated after a walk—and that I had given her medication. Despite this, Dr. Daly showed no empathy and, in what felt like a xenophobic attitude, did not examine my dog. She just held Judite’s snout briefly and scheduled the surgery. No basic tests were done, even though I paid for the consultation.

On the way home, Judite had a seizure in the car. I rushed back to the clinic, and only then was she examined. They told me she had a fever of 43°C.
If Dr. Glen Daly had done her job—had she listened, cared, or simply treated my dog like a life that mattered—Judite might still be alive.
